paper_metadata.title: Quantum Speedups for Derivative Pricing: Beyond Black-Scholes

summary: This paper is a purely theoretical resource analysis of gate-based quantum derivative pricing. It claims asymptotic quadratic speedups for CIR and a restricted Heston model, and for quantum MLMC with bipartite correlations, with resource bounds such as eO(poly(T, B)/epsilon) gates for CIR and eO(poly(d, T, B)/epsilon) gates for Heston, but reports no hardware experiments or numerical benchmarks.

experiments.description: Theoretical gate-based quantum Monte Carlo pricing over the Cox–Ingersoll–Ross (CIR) process using fast-forwarding, with resource analysis for loading the discretized path distribution and pricing a piecewise-linear payoff.

algorithm.variant: vanilla quantum Monte Carlo integration with fast-forwarded CIR state preparation

hyperparameters.r: degrees of freedom for chi-square primitive

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Discrete qsample over truncated and discretized primitive distributions (standard Gaussian and central chi-square) for the CIR path increments; payoff encoded via amplitude rotation.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate E[f(\u1e8bV) | V(0)=v0] for a piecewise-linear payoff f over a CIR path process.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Truncation to bounded intervals and Riemann-sum discretization; no QUBO/Ising constraints.

problem_instance.description: Derivative pricing over a single CIR process with T monitoring points; path-dependent piecewise-linear payoff.
problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Not applicable; synthetic stochastic-process model with truncation and discretization of primitive distributions.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Asymptotic resource analysis; no numerical benchmark runs reported.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Truncate Gaussian and chi-square primitives; discretize with N grid points; recursively compute CIR transition map.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Amplitude estimation on the encoded payoff probability/amplitude.

results.value: O(T2 log2(N) log(T) + T(b + r) log(N) log(BTb/epsilon) + log3(BTbN) + N_f)
O(T^2 log^2(N) log(T) + T(b + r) log(N) log(BTb/epsilon) + log^3(BTbN) + N_f)

speedup_claims.conditions: for a piecewise-linear payoff over a single CIR process with fast-forwarded state preparation; asymptotic resource analysis
speedup_claims.caveats: No numerical benchmark or hardware experiment; speedup is asymptotic and depends on truncation/discretization being controlled.

speedup_claims.conditions: resource analysis for gate-based quantum Monte Carlo pricing over the CIR process; asymptotic scaling with truncation/discretization parameters
speedup_claims.caveats: No numerical benchmark runs; this is a theoretical resource estimate.

advantage_assessment.crossover_size: Not assessed; no empirical crossover analysis is reported.
advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: The paper gives asymptotic resources for CIR pricing: eO(poly(T, B)/epsilon) gates and O(poly(T)) qubits, with Theorem 6.1 giving O(T^2 log^2(N) log(T) + T(b+r) log(N) log(BTb/epsilon) + log^3(BTbN) + N_f) gates and O(T log(N)) qubits.

notes: The paper is a theoretical resource analysis; no actual hardware execution, simulator, or benchmark data are reported.
Gate count and qubit scaling are taken from Theorem 6.1 / Theorem 6.3 and surrounding text.
The paper claims an end-to-end quadratic speedup for CIR pricing, but only in asymptotic resource analysis.
No benchmark or hardware result is reported.

experiments.description: Theoretical gate-based quantum Monte Carlo pricing over the multi-asset Heston model with asset-asset correlations only, using fast-forwarding and loading of Gaussian, chi-square, and CIR-integral primitives.

algorithm.variant: vanilla quantum Monte Carlo integration with fast-forwarded multi-asset Heston state preparation

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Discrete qsample over truncated and discretized primitives for Heston path increments: standard Gaussians, chi-square variables, CIR-integral conditional distribution, and additional Gaussians for correlated asset shocks.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate E[f(\u1e8bS) | S(0)=s0, V(0)=v0] for a piecewise-linear payoff f over the multi-asset Heston path process.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Truncation to bounded regions and discretization; no QUBO/Ising constraints.

problem_instance.description: Derivative pricing over a d-asset Heston model with asset-asset correlations only and T monitoring points; path-dependent piecewise-linear payoff.
problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Not applicable; synthetic stochastic-process model with truncation and discretization of primitive distributions.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Asymptotic resource analysis; no numerical benchmark runs reported.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Load CIR primitives, then compute Heston increments and exponentiate the accumulated log-price update.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Amplitude estimation on the encoded payoff probability/amplitude.

speedup_claims.conditions: for the multi-asset Heston model with asset-asset correlations only, piecewise-linear payoff, and asymptotic fast-forwarded state preparation
speedup_claims.caveats: No empirical benchmark; the result is conditional on the model-parameter regime where truncation bounds are finite.

speedup_claims.conditions: gate-based quantum Monte Carlo pricing over the multi-asset Heston model with asymptotic resource analysis
speedup_claims.caveats: No empirical comparison; only asymptotic scaling is reported.

advantage_assessment.crossover_size: Not assessed; no empirical crossover analysis is reported.
advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: The paper gives asymptotic resources for Heston pricing: eO(poly(d, T, B)/epsilon) gates and O(poly(T)) qubits, with Theorem 6.4 / 6.6 indicating polynomial-in-(d,T) overhead and O(dT log(N)) qubits for state preparation.

notes: The paper is a theoretical resource analysis; no actual hardware execution, simulator, or benchmark data are reported.
Gate count and qubit scaling are taken from Theorem 6.4 / Theorem 6.6 and surrounding text.
The paper claims an end-to-end quadratic speedup for a restricted Heston model, but only asymptotically.
No benchmark or hardware result is reported.

experiments.description: Theoretical gate-based quantum multi-level Monte Carlo (MLMC) pricing for correlated SDEs with bipartite correlations, using a quantum Milstein sampler and two-dimensional Lévy-area loading.

algorithm.variant: quantum MLMC with quantum Milstein sampler for (d,2)-Milstein sampling

hyperparameters.N_ell: number of quantum samples per level

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Encode Brownian increments and selected Lévy areas (for bipartite correlations) into a qsample for the Milstein update; payoff evaluated on the coupled fine/coarse paths.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate E[f(X)] for a globally Lipschitz payoff f under approximate SDE simulation with Milstein discretization and MLMC telescoping sum.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: No QUBO constraints; truncation/discretization of primitive distributions and coupling of fine/coarse levels in MLMC.

problem_instance.description: Globally Lipschitz derivative pricing over a correlated SDE with bipartite correlations; approximate simulation via Milstein and MLMC.
problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Not applicable; synthetic stochastic-process model with truncation and discretization of Gaussian and Lévy-area primitives.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Asymptotic analysis of MLMC variance and gate complexity; no numerical benchmark runs reported.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Couple fine and coarse Milstein paths; load Gaussian and two-dimensional Lévy-area primitives; evaluate telescoping differences.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Quantum amplitude estimation within each MLMC level.

speedup_claims.baseline_method: classical multi-level Monte Carlo / classical Monte Carlo integration
speedup_claims.conditions: globally Lipschitz payoff, approximate SDE simulation with Milstein scheme, and bipartite correlations enabling (d,2)-Milstein sampling
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper notes this does not extend to arbitrary correlations; the result is asymptotic and relies on efficient two-dimensional Lévy-area loading.

speedup_claims.baseline_method: classical multilevel Monte Carlo / classical Monte Carlo
speedup_claims.conditions: MLMC pricing for correlated SDEs with (d,2)-Milstein sampling and two-dimensional Lévy-area loading
speedup_claims.caveats: The result is asymptotic and theoretical; no benchmark data are reported.

advantage_assessment.crossover_size: Not assessed; no empirical crossover analysis is reported.
advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: The paper gives an asymptotic quantum MLMC result for bipartite-correlated SDEs: eO(poly(T, d) sigma0/epsilon) gates and O(poly(T, d, log(sigma0/epsilon))) qubits.
limiting_factors: Need for Milstein and Lévy-area loading

notes: The paper is a theoretical resource analysis; no actual hardware execution, simulator, or benchmark data are reported.
The MLMC result is Theorem 7.2; the paper emphasizes bipartite correlations and (d,2)-Milstein sampling.
The paper claims an end-to-end quadratic speedup for quantum MLMC under bipartite correlations.
No benchmark or hardware result is reported.
